title: The save file
concept: Files · open, read and write text
description: Read the scores the game saved, line by line, and write a summary file of your own.

tasks.title: Read and write a file
tasks.body: with open("notes.txt") as f: opens a file and closes it again when the block ends. f.read() gives all its text, and for line in f: goes through it a line at a time, each line still ending in its newline.
tasks.detail: open("log.txt", "w") opens a file for writing and wipes what was there; "a" adds to the end instead. f.write("text\n") writes text, and the newline is yours to add. line.strip() removes the newline and any spaces at each end. Files here are temporary: they exist only while your program runs.

tasks.code:
# Read the quest log, then add to it
with open("quests.txt") as f:
    for line in f:
        print("-", line.strip())

with open("quests.txt", "a") as f:
    f.write("Rest at the inn\n")

with open("quests.txt") as f:
    print(len(f.readlines()), "quests now")
tasks.output:
- Find the key
- Cross the river
- Open the gate
4 quests now
tasks.note: strip() takes the newline off each line before printing. "a" added a fourth quest at the end, and reading the file again counts it.

files.quests.txt:

tasks.question: What would the last line say if the second open() used "w" instead of "a"?
tasks.why: "w" wipes the file before writing, so only the new quest is left in it.

tasks.prompt: Predict, then run: change "a" to "w". Then print each line without strip(), and look at the gaps that appear.

The game saves its scores in scores.txt, one whole number per line, and some lines may be blank or hold only spaces. Read the file and print three lines: how many scores there are, the highest score, and the total. Then write the total, on a line of its own, into a new file called summary.txt, and print what summary.txt holds, read back from the file.
hints: Open scores.txt inside a with block, and go through it a line at a time. strip() each line, and skip it if nothing is left.
Keep the scores in a list as whole numbers, then len(), max() and sum() do the rest. Open summary.txt with "w", write the total and a newline, then read it back in a second with block.
With other names: with open("names.txt") as f: then for row in f: and name = row.strip() inside the loop.

error_hints.text: The file name must match exactly: scores.txt, all in lowercase, with no folder before it.
Make the list of scores before the loop that fills it, and spell it the same way every time.
int() could not read a line. A blank line, or one holding only spaces, has to be skipped before int().
f.write() takes text: turn the total into text with str() first.
With 10, 40 and 25 in the file, the lines are 3, 40, 75, and 75 again, read back from summary.txt.
Blank lines are not scores: skip them, and count only the lines with a number.
A file with one score and no newline at the end still has one score.
Check a longer file: every line with a number counts.
Check a line holding only spaces: after strip() it is empty, so it is skipped too.

similar_example.code:
with open("names.txt", "w") as f:
    f.write("Ada\n\nBen\n")
with open("names.txt") as f:
    for row in f:
        name = row.strip()
        if name:
            print(name)
similar_example.note: Writing a file, then reading it back and skipping the blank line. Your program reads numbers, and writes a summary of them.

other_ways.code:
with open("scores.txt") as f:
    scores = [int(word) for word in f.read().split()]
print(len(scores))
print(max(scores))
print(sum(scores))
with open("summary.txt", "w") as f:
    print(sum(scores), file=f)
with open("summary.txt") as f:
    print(f.read().strip())
other_ways.note: split() with no argument splits on any run of spaces and newlines, so blank lines vanish on their own. print(..., file=f) writes a line to a file.

other_ways.code:
total = 0
count = 0
best = None
for line in open("scores.txt"):
    if line.strip() == "":
        continue
    score = int(line)
    count += 1
    total += score
    if best is None or score > best:
        best = score
print(count)
print(best)
print(total)
open("summary.txt", "w").write(f"{total}\n")
print(open("summary.txt").read().strip())
other_ways.note: Without with, the files close when Python is done with them. with is safer, because it closes the file even when something goes wrong.
